sentences.text: Unwindia was a pterodactyloid pterosaur that inhabited the Early Cretaceous period in present-day Brazil.
The fossil record preserves a snout fragment measuring exactly 221 mm in length.
This animal possessed a unique arrangement of seven pairs of teeth positioned entirely forward of the nasoantorbital fenestra.
Unlike other Santana Formation pterosaurs, its dentition was homodont, featuring long, straight, conical teeth slightly flattened sideways that reached up to 9 mm.

The holotype specimen, defined as the specific example used to describe the species, was acquired by the German State Museum of Natural History Karlsruhe from an illegal digger near Santana do Cariri in the Araripe Basin.
David Martill formally named and described the species Unwindia trigonus in 2011.
The genus name Unwindia pays tribute to the British pterosaur expert David Unwin.
Unwindia is classified within the superfamily Ctenochasmatoidea.
David Martill concluded that Unwindia was a basal ctenochasmatoid without performing a phylogenetic analysis.
Mark Witton suggested in 2013 that Unwindia might belong to the family Lonchodectidae.
However, in 2020, Alexander Averianov argued that Unwindia does not belong to the family Lonchodectidae.
Consequently, the family classification for Unwindia remains uncertain and is listed as possibly Lonchodectidae.
The holotype was recovered from the Santana Formation of the Araripe Basin, a site dated to the Cenomanian stage.
The estimated time range for Unwindia spans between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
